transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I haven’t really been myself since my friend from choir passed away so suddenly. We used to sit together, and she always knew who was bringing what to the church potlucks—funny the things you miss, you know?

Now I’ll be looking at a potluck list and just start crying, or I get all worked up over phone calls I used to handle without thinking. And I’ve started missing church planning things, which… that’s not like me. I never would’ve missed those before.

{"intent": "Determine if the patient's symptoms are related to Bereavement (F43.22) versus Major Depressive Episode (F32.0) versus Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood (F43.11) by assessing the duration and onset of symptoms in relation to the bereavement."}

It started after she died — that was just about a month ago now. It was so sudden, and I think that’s when I really began falling apart with the church planning. Before that, I was keeping up with things fine… well, as fine as anyone does, I guess. You know, those sign-up sheets can be a whole ordeal on their own.
Are these feelings happening mostly when you’re reminded of your friend, or do they come up even when you’re not thinking about her?

Mostly when something reminds me of her, I think… like the potluck lists, that’ll just set me off crying because she always knew who was doing what. But then it spills over, too. I’ll get all worked up about phone calls I used to handle easy, and then I don’t go to the church planning things at all—which I never would’ve missed before.

It’s just since she passed so suddenly, I haven’t really felt like myself.
Are there times when you’re not reminded of your friend where you still feel down or overwhelmed, or does it only happen when something brings her to mind?

It’s mostly tied to her, I suppose… or at least it started that way. Like those potluck lists, I’ll see one and just start crying because she was always the one who knew who was bringing the casseroles and who’d forget the rolls—oh, and she had this way of teasing people about it without making anyone feel bad.

But then, even when I’m not exactly thinking of her, I still get all worked up. Phone calls I used to handle without a second thought feel like too much now, and I’ve been missing church planning things I never would’ve missed before. Ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or ability to concentrate, even when you're not reminded of your friend?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed it in that neat of a way, you know? I mean, some days I feel worn out, but then I think, well, everyone gets worn out when things are happening at church and there’s a million little things to keep straight.

Appetite and sleep… I don’t know. I haven’t really been keeping track. I’ll start to answer and then I think about whether I remembered to call someone back about the setup tables, and then I’m off worrying about that instead. So I guess I can’t say for sure.
Are there times when you're not thinking about your friend or reminders of her where you still feel down, tearful, or like you don’t have the energy to do things?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it started with things that reminded me of her—those potluck lists especially, I’ll just cry because she always handled them so easily. But even when I’m not sitting there thinking about her, I’m still not myself.

I get all worked up over phone calls I used to do without any trouble, and then I don’t go to the church planning meetings, which… that’s not like me at all. I never would’ve missed those before. Since she passed so suddenly, everything just feels harder to manage.
Have you noticed that these feelings are affecting parts of your life outside of church or things related to your friend, like your relationships at home, your work, or other daily activities?

Well… outside of church, I’m not sure I’ve thought about it that way. Most of what I notice is with the church things, because that’s where she and I were always tangled up together, you know?

But it has affected things. I’ve had to let other church members take over the calls and the lists, and parts of the luncheon too, because I’m just not keeping up the way I always did. I used to know who needed calling and what had to be written down, and now I’ll start one thing and then—well, it just gets away from me. That’s been hard to admit.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or ability to function in areas of your life outside of church or grief-related reminders, such as at home, with family, or in your personal activities?

I guess at home I don’t notice it the same way, or maybe I just don’t pay attention to it there. The church things are what show it the most. I mean, I used to have all those calls and lists in my head—who needed reminding, who was bringing what, all of that—and now I’ve had to let other people take over some of it, even parts of the luncheon.

And that sounds small maybe, but for me that was just… what I did. I always kept up with it before. Lately I just haven’t been able to keep it all straight.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or ability to cope with everyday tasks outside of the church or grief-related situations—like at home, with family, or in your personal routines?

I’m… not really sure. I keep trying to think of something at home that’s different, but my mind goes right back to the church things, because that’s where I notice it.

At home I suppose I just go about things, or I don’t pay much attention. My sister called the other day—well, not my sister, my cousin, I always mix those two up because they both call around supper time—and we were talking about who was making potato salad for something, and then I started thinking about the luncheon again. So it all kind of circles back there.

I don’t know that I can say clearly about personal routines. I haven’t really separated it out that way.
Do you ever feel down, overwhelmed, or have trouble managing tasks even when you’re not thinking about your friend or anything related to the church?

I don’t know that I could say for sure. When I feel overwhelmed, it usually has some thread back to the church, or to her, even if it starts as something else.

Like yesterday I was just folding towels, and then I remembered I still hadn’t written down who was supposed to bring rolls, and then I was back in it again. So is that “not thinking about it,” or did it just sneak in? I’m not sure.

I haven’t really noticed myself feeling down out of nowhere, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like everything keeps circling back to the same place.
Can you think of a time in the past week when you felt down, tearful, or overwhelmed that wasn’t connected to your friend or anything related to the church?

I’m trying to think, but honestly, most of the times I got tearful this week had something tied to her or the church.

Like, I cried over those potluck lists, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud. I used to handle all those calls and who’s bringing what without even thinking, and now I get all worked up and lose track. I even missed one of the planning things I never would’ve missed before.

Ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. Even if I start out doing something ordinary, it seems to come back around to that.

Can you recall any moment in the past week where you felt down, tearful, or overwhelmed while doing something completely unrelated to your friend or the church, like a personal hobby, watching TV, or doing household chores?

I’m trying to picture it… like watching TV or doing chores, but honestly it doesn’t stay separate for long.

I’ll be doing something normal, and then I think of the potluck lists, or who I was supposed to call, and I get all worked up. I know that sounds small, but I used to do those calls so easily. Now I cry over the lists, and I’ve even missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.

Ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just… I haven’t been myself. Even when it starts as household things, it seems to wander right back there.
Can you recall a time in the past week when you felt down, tearful, or overwhelmed that was not related to grief or church-related responsibilities?

Not really… I keep trying to separate it out, but it all seems to lead back there somehow.

Ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I’ll start with something simple, like those potluck lists, and then I’m crying over them. Or I get all worked up about calls I used to make without even thinking twice. And I’ve missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.

So I can’t honestly think of a time this week where it was just… unrelated. It all seems tangled up together.
Would you say that your sadness and difficulty functioning are mainly limited to situations related to your friend's death, or have they become more widespread in your daily life?

I think it’s mostly tied to her passing and the church things, but it’s also kind of spilling into my day more than I expected.

Ever since my choir friend died so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I’ll look at something like the potluck lists, and I get teary, which feels silly because I used to handle all that without a second thought. And the calls, too — I’d call people, organize things, remember who was bringing what. Now I get all worked up over it.

I even missed a church planning thing, and that’s not like me at all. I’ve always been someone people could count on for those things. So… I guess it started with her death, but it’s affecting how I’m managing those everyday responsibilities connected to it.

Would you say that your sadness and difficulty functioning only happen in situations related to your friend’s death, or have they started affecting areas of your life that aren’t connected to her or the church?

It’s hard for me to say it’s completely outside of her or the church, because that’s where it keeps circling back to.

Ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I’ll sit down with the potluck lists, something I used to do without thinking, and suddenly I’m crying over it. Or I’ll need to make calls, and I get all worked up, even though those used to be easy for me. I’ve even missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.

So… I guess it started with her death, but it’s affecting how I’m handling those things now. I don’t feel like myself.
